Rashi on Shabbat 76a:1:1.hebrew: א"ר אלעזר הא - דקתני מתניתין: דאינו כשר להצניע והצניעו אחר, הוא מתחייב על הוצאתו, וכל אדם פטורין — דלא כר' שמעון בן אלעזר:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:1:1.english: Rabbi Elazar said: This - That which the Mishnah teaches: that [regarding an item that] is not fit to be stored and someone stored it, he is liable for carrying it out, and all [other] people are exempt — [this is] not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:2:2.hebrew: כמלא פי גמל - נפיש שיעורא מפי פרה. אבל כמלא פי פרה לא מיחייב, דהא לא חזו לפרה:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:2:2.english: Equivalent to a camel’s mouthful - [This] measure is larger than a cow’s mouthful. But for a cow’s mouthful he is not liable, since it is not suitable for a cow.

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:2:4.hebrew: פי טלה - נפיש מפי גדי. הלכך, עמיר, דלא חזי לגדי, לא מיחייב כמלא פי גדי עד דאיכא מלא פי טלה. אבל עשבים, הואיל וחזו בין לטלה בין לגדי, מיחייב אפי' כמלא פי גדי:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:2:4.english: A lamb’s mouth - Is larger than a kid’s mouth. Therefore, [for] stalks of grain, which are not suitable for a kid, one is not liable for a kid’s mouthful until there is a lamb’s mouthful. But [for] grass, since it is suitable both for a lamb and for a kid, one is liable even for a kid’s mouthful.

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:2:5.hebrew: לחין - הראויין לאדם — כגרוגרת, דזה שיעור לכל מאכל אדם לשבת. אבל כמלא פי גדי — לא, דלחים לא חזו לגדי:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:2:5.english: Moist - [Those] that are fit for human consumption — [the measure is] equivalent to a dried fig, as this is the measure for all human food for Shabbat. But [to be liable for] equivalent to a goat’s mouthful — no, as moist [leaves] are not fit for a goat.

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:3:1.hebrew: המוציא תבן כמלא פי פרה - והוציאו להאכילו לגמל, שפי גמל גדול מפי פרה:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:3:1.english: One who carries out straw equivalent to a cow’s mouthful - And he carried it out to feed it to a camel, for a camel’s mouth is larger than a cow’s mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:3:2.hebrew: דהא חזי לפי פרה - הלכך שיעור חשוב הוא, ולכל מי שיוציאנו לא פקע שיעוריה בהכי:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:3:2.english: As it is suitable for a cow’s mouth - Therefore, it is a significant measure, and for anyone who carries it out, its measure does not lapse on account of this.

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:4:1.hebrew: דחייב - דהאיכא שיעורא דחזי לפרה, הלכך כשר להצניע הוא ומצניעין כמוהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:4:1.english: That he is liable - For behold, there is a measure that is fit for a cow; therefore, it is fit for storage, and [people] store [quantities] like it:

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:4:2.hebrew: עצה - לא חזיא לפרה אלא ע"י הדחק, אלא לגמל הוא דחזי, וזה הוציאו לפרה:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:4:2.english: Etza - It is not fit for a cow except in a time of pressing need; rather, it is fit for a camel, and this [person] carried it out for a cow.

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:5:1.hebrew: רבי יוחנן אמר פטור - דהא לגמל דחזי ליה ליכא שיעורא, ואי משום דלצורך פרה הוציאו ולגבה איכא שיעור — אכילה ע"י הדחק לאו אכילה היא. הלכך, לא משערי' ליה בפרה:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:5:1.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: He is exempt - For regarding a camel, for which it is fit, there is not the [requisite] measure; and if [one would suggest liability] because he carried it out for the needs of a cow, and regarding it there is the [requisite] measure — eating under duress is not [considered] eating. Therefore, we do not measure it by a cow.

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:7:1.hebrew: אין מצטרפין לחמור שבהם - מי ששיעורו גדול הוי קל, ואינו מצטרף להשלים שיעורו של חמור, דהא לא חשיב כי ההוא. אבל החשוב משלים את הקל לכשיעור: תבן מצטרף עם עצה להשלי' פי גמל, ועצה אין מצטרף עם התבן להשלים מלא פי פרה:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:7:1.english: They do not join together to the more stringent among them - That whose measure is large is [considered] lenient, and does not join to complete the measure of the stringent [substance], as it is not as significant as that one. But the significant [substance] completes the lenient [one] to [its] measure: straw joins with etza to complete a camel's mouthful, but etza does not join with straw to complete a cow's full mouthful.

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:8:1.english: Do they join together - Even for the [more] stringent [item] to complete the [more] lenient [one]?

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:8:2.hebrew: ג' על ג' - לטומאת מדרס הזב, ליעשות אב הטומאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:8:2.english: Three by three [handbreadths] - For the midras impurity of a zav, to become a primary source of ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:8:3.hebrew: הבגד והשק מצטרפין - שהבגד משלים שיעור השק. שק עשוי מנוצה של עזים:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:8:3.english: The garment and the sack join together - That the garment completes the measure of the sack. A sack is made from goats’ hair.

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:8:4.hebrew: ואמר ר' שמעון מה טעם - מצטרפין:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:8:4.english: And Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason - [That they] join together?

Rashi on Shabbat 76a:8:5.hebrew: הואיל וראויין ליטמא מושב - אם צירף משנים יחד לטלאי מרדעת של חמור כשיעורו לענין מושב הזב — אם קצע משנים מהן ותקן טפח על טפח לישב עליו — מיטמא ליה אב הטומאה במושב הזב, דתניא: "המקצע מכולן טפח על טפח — טמא מושב". ואמרינן טעמא בפ"ק דסוכה: הואיל וראוי לטלות על גבי חמור, שאינו מקפיד אם הוא משני מינין:
Rashi on Shabbat 76a:8:5.english: Since they are fit to become ritually impure [as] a seat - If one combined [pieces] from two [different materials] together for a patch on a donkey's pack-saddle according to its measure with regard to the seat of a zav — if he cut from two of them and prepared [a patch of] a handbreadth by a handbreadth to sit upon it — it becomes defiled for him as a primary source of ritual impurity through [being] the seat of a zav. For it is taught [in a baraita]: "One who cuts from all of them [pieces totaling] a handbreadth by a handbreadth — it is ritually impure [as] a seat." And we state the reason in the first chapter of Sukkah: Since it is fit to patch upon the back of a donkey, for [the owner] is not particular if it is of two kinds.

Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:2:1.hebrew: מפני שלא שוו בשיעוריהם - אבל אותם ששוו, כגון עמיר ועלי שום ועלי בצלים לחים — מצטרפין. וכן חמור לקל, כגון תבן לעצה — למלא פי גמל; ואפי' לא יהא תבן ראוי לגמל, שמא אגב העצה הוא ראוי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:2:1.english: "Because they are not equal in their measures" - But those that are equal, such as ears of grain, and moist garlic leaves and onion leaves, join together. And similarly, [a substance with a more] stringent [measure joins] to [one with a more] lenient [measure], such as straw to etza, to [complete] a camel’s mouthful; and even if straw is not fit for a camel, perhaps along with the etza it is fit.

Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:5:1.hebrew: אכילה ע"י הדחק לא שמה אכילה - והא דאמר בפ' כיצד הרגל (ב"ק דף יט.): "אכילה ע"י הדחק שמה אכילה" — ה"מ לענין ניזקין, דלא חשבינן ליה משונה; אבל לאחשובה לענין שבת, לא חשיבא אכילה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:5:1.english: Eating under duress is not considered eating - And as for that which is said in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad HaRegel (Bava Kamma 19b): "Eating under duress is considered eating" — this applies [only] with regard to damages, where we do not consider it unusual; but to consider it [significant] with regard to Shabbat, it is not considered eating.

Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:6:1.hebrew: אידי ואידי חד שיעורא הוא - והא דנקט במתני' כמלא פי טלה ולא נקט כגרוגרת — לאשמעי' דמשום אכילת טלה נתנו בו חכמים שיעור זה; דאי נקט כגרוגרת, לא הוה ידעינן למה נתנו בו חכמים שיעור זה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:6:1.english: "This and that are one measure" - And that which [the Tanna] taught in the Mishnah, "equivalent to a lamb’s mouthful," and did not teach "equivalent to a dried fig-bulk" — [this was] to teach us that [it was] on account of a lamb’s eating that the Sages established this measure for it; for had he taught "equivalent to a dried fig-bulk," we would not have known why the Sages established this measure for it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:8:1.hebrew: הבגד והשק השק והעור כו' - דוקא בכה"ג: הבגד והשק, השק והעור; אבל הבגד והעור, והשק והמפץ — אין מצטרפין, שאין ראויין להתחבר יחד, והמחברן בטלה דעתו, ואין טמאים מדרס. ר"י:
Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:8:1.english: "The garment and the sack, the sack and the hide, etc." - Specifically in this manner: the garment and the sack, [or] the sack and the hide; but the garment and the hide, or the sack and the mat, do not join together, as they are not fit to be joined together, and [as for] one who joins them, his intention is disregarded, and they are not susceptible to midras impurity. — Ri.

Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:8:2.hebrew: ואמר ר"ש מה טעם כו' - תימה לר"י: דמה צריך להאי טעמא? דהא כיון דמצטרפין זה עם זה, א"כ ראוי לחברן וחזו למדרס; וכיון דחזו למדרס, פשיטא דמצטרפין לטומאת מדרס, דהא אפ' כופת שאור שיחדה לישיבה טמאה מדרס, כדאמרינן בהעור והרוטב (חולין קכט.). והכא בטומאת מדרס איירי, מדקאמר "הבגד שלשה על שלשה", דלענין טומאת מת אפ' ג' על ג', כדפרישית לעיל. ואור"י: דודאי הא דקתני "הבגד שלשה על שלשה" לא מיירי אלא למדרס, אבל סיפא דשק ואור ומפץ מיירי נמי בטומאת מת. והכי איתא במס' כלים בפכ"ז: "הבגד שלשה על שלשה [למדרס ומשום ג' על ג'] לטומאת מת, השק ד' על ד', העור ה' על ה', המפץ ו' על ו' — שוו בין למדרס בין לטמא מת", אלא שהש"ס מביאה בקוצר, כמו שרגיל בכמה מקומות. ועל טומאת מת קאמר: מה טעם מצטרפין — בשלא יחדו למדרס. ולא צריך האי טעמא אצירוף דעור ומפץ, דמפץ לא מטמא במת אלא כשטמא בזב, דהיינו כשיחדו למדרס, ומק"ו דפכין קטנים, כדאמרינן בפ' ר' עקיבא (לקמן שבת פד:):
Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:8:2.english: "And Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason etc." - The Ri finds this puzzling: Why is this reason necessary? For since they join together with one another, if so, they are suitable to be joined together and are fit for midras [sitting upon]; and once they are fit for midras, it is obvious that they join together for midras impurity, for even a block of sourdough that one designated for sitting becomes impure with midras impurity, as we say in [the chapter] HaOr VehaRotev (Chullin 129a). And here [the baraita] is dealing with midras impurity, since it states, "The garment [must be] three by three [handbreadths]," for regarding corpse impurity, even three by three [fingerbreadths is susceptible], as I explained earlier. And the Ri says: Indeed, that which is taught, "The garment [must be] three by three," is dealing only with midras, but the latter clause of sack, leather, and matting is dealing with corpse impurity as well. And so it is found in Tractate Kelim in chapter 27: "The garment is three by three [for midras, and three by three] for corpse impurity; the sack is four by four, the leather five by five, [and] the matting six by six — they are equal whether for midras or for corpse impurity." Rather, the Shas quotes it abridged, as it is accustomed [to do] in several places. And it is regarding corpse impurity that [Rabbi Shimon] says: What is the reason they join together? — [namely,] in a case where one did not designate them for midras. And this reason is not needed regarding the combination of leather and matting, for matting does not become impure with corpse impurity except when it is impure through a zav — that is, when one designated it for midras — and [derived] by an a fortiori argument (kal vaḥomer) from small jugs, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Akiva (below, Shabbat 84b).

Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:8:3.hebrew: הואיל וראויין ליטמא מושב - פי' בקונטרס: אם קיצע משנים וצירף יחד לטלאי מרדעת החמור; וההיא ד"המקצע מכולם טפח על טפח" דמעילה — היינו שבין כולם יש טפח. ואין נראה לר"י, דמה צריך להביא ראיה שראויין להצטרף? בלאו טעמא דמושב נמי שמעינן ממתני' דהכא שראויין להצטרף יחד באותו סדר כמו ששנויים — בגד לשק, ושק לעור, ועור למפץ — דדוקא נקט, לפי שאלו ראויין להצטרף יחד! ונראה לר"י כמו שפי' ריב"א, ד"הואיל וראויין ליטמא מושב" היינו הואיל ושוו שיעוריהן לענין מושב. וכמו שפירש בקונטרס בפ"ק דסוכה (דף יז:): ד"המקצע מכולן" היינו מאיזה מהן שיקצע יהא טמא; ואע"ג שכאן אין שיעורן שוה — מצטרפין, הואיל ולענין מושב שיעורן שוה. והא דקאמר: "ה"נ חזו לדוגמא" — היינו נמי דשיעורן שוה לדוגמא, כדתנן בפרק המצניע דלדוגמא כל שהוא; הלכך מצטרפין אפי' לענין דבר דלא שוו שיעורייהו. וה"ה דהוי מצי למינקט הכא: "ולזרע ולרפואה", דהוו נמי בכל שהוא; אלא דלא כל דברים שייך בהו זרע ורפואה, אבל דוגמא שייכא בכל דבר. והא דקאמר בסוכה: "המקצע מכולן כו' הואיל וראוי לטלות על גבי חמורו" — לשון "הואיל וראוי" לאו דווקא, דדווקא אם עשה מהן טלאי ויחדן לכך טמא בטפח על טפח. וכן מצינו לקמן בפ' א"ר עקיבא (שבת דף צ.): "הואיל וראויין למתק הקדרה", דהוה ליה למימר "הואיל וממתקין", דהא מיירי שנפלו לתוך הקדרה. ר"י:
Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:8:3.english: Since they are fit to become ritually impure [as] a seat - The Kuntres explained: If one cut [pieces] from two [materials] and joined [them] together for a patch of a donkey's pack-saddle; and that [teaching] of "one who cuts from all of them a handbreadth by a handbreadth" in Me'ilah means that among all of them there is a handbreadth. And this does not appear correct to the Ri, for why does [the Gemara] need to bring a proof that they are fit to join together? Even without the rationale of a seat, we also learn from our Mishnah here that they are fit to join together in that order as they are taught: garment to sack, sack to hide, and hide to mat — which it specifically stated because these are fit to join together! And it appears to the Ri as Riva explained: that "since they are fit to become ritually impure [as] a seat" means since their measures are equal regarding [the impurity of] a seat. And as the Kuntres explained in the first chapter of Sukkah (17b): that "one who cuts from all of them" means from whichever of them he cuts, it will be ritually impure; and even though here their measures are not equal, they join together since regarding a seat their measures are equal. And that which [Rava] says: "Here too, they are suited for a sample" — that also means that their measures are equal for a sample, as we learned in the chapter [entitled] "Hamatznia" that for a sample [the measure for liability is] any amount; therefore, they join together even regarding a matter where their measures are not equal. And the same applies [that the Gemara] could have mentioned here: "and for seed, and for medicine," which are also [subject to liability for] any amount; however, seed and medicine do not apply to all things, whereas a sample applies to everything. And that which [the Gemara] says in Sukkah: "One who cuts from all of them, etc., since it is fit to patch on his donkey" — the phrasing "since it is fit" is not precise, for specifically if he made a patch from them and designated them for this is it ritually impure at a handbreadth by a handbreadth. And similarly we find below in the chapter [entitled] "Amar Rabbi Akiva" (Shabbat 90a): "since they are fit to sweeten the pot," where it should have said "since they sweeten," for it is dealing with [a case where] they fell into the pot. Ri.

Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:8:4.hebrew: תוספתא - המקצע למשכב: אין פחות משלשה על שלשה; למושב — טפח; ולמעמד — כל שהוא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 76a:8:4.english: Tosefta: One who cuts [a patch] for [an article used for] lying upon, [its measure is] no less than three by three [handbreadths]; for [an article used for] sitting upon, a handbreadth; and for a stand [i.e., a finger-guard for gripping], any amount.
